summary.headline: Punjab & Sind Bank posts record FY26 net profit of Rs.1,322 crore (up 30.12%) and total business of Rs.2,63,652 crore (up 14.94%).
summary.overview: FY26 showed record net profit of Rs.1,322 crore, up 30.12%, with Q4 net profit of Rs.422 crore, up 34.82% YoY. Gross advances grew 18.29% and deposits 12.37%, with business growing 14.94% to Rs.2,63,652 crore. Asset quality improved on a full-year basis (Gross NPA 2.40%, Net NPA 0.79%), but Q4 slippages rose to Rs.355 crore from Rs.168 crore in Q3, mainly from MSME accounts. Net interest margin for the year was 2.55%, and management guided it to 2.65-2.70% by FY27 end. Management also flagged RBI's ECL framework, which it expects to absorb through a five-year glide path with capital impact of roughly Rs.600-800 crore (CRO's preliminary estimate).

segments.name: Retail, Agriculture and MSME (RAM)
segments.commentary: RAM is nearly 59% of advances, with retail growing over 24%, agriculture over 23% and MSME over 29%. MSME is where residual stress was recognised in Q4, and management says it will keep the RAM share above 60% in FY27.

segments.name: Corporate
segments.commentary: Corporate pipeline stands at around Rs.18,000 crore, up from Rs.10,000-12,000 crore discussed last time. Management is selective on pricing and churns the portfolio across AAA, AA and A rated borrowers.

segments.name: Co-lending and gold loans
segments.commentary: Co-lending platform is over Rs.10,000 crore with about 11 partners. Gold loan book is growing over 100% organically, with expansion also planned through NBFC co-lending.

segments.name: Housing and vehicle finance
segments.commentary: About 85 housing builder tie-ups were done in FY26. Vehicle tie-ups are with Mahindra and Maruti, with Hyundai and Toyota under pursuit. A second-hand vehicle digital product is at pipeline stage, and the portfolio is still small.

guidance_outlook: FY27 deposit growth guided at 13-14%, advances growth at 16-18%, and RAM share above 60% of advances.
Gross NPA to be below 2% and PCR maintained at 92-93%. Management said it fell just short of FY26 net NPA and PCR guidance but expects to meet all targets in FY27.
Recovery and upgradation to cross Rs.1,000 crore in FY27. Credit cost and slippage ratio to stay below 1%.
NIM expected to reach 2.65-2.70% by end of FY27, helped by higher-yielding retail, agri and MSME mix and no imminent rate cut.
Aspiration of Rs.3,00,000 crore business in the current year and Rs.4,00,000 crore by FY29 (board-approved), requiring about Rs.50,000 crore added per year.

ECL framework to be phased over five years through FY31, with EIR applicable from FY30. Capital impact estimated at Rs.600-800 crore, to be absorbed from capital buffers. Final calculations still pending.
GIFT City branch targeted for launch by October 2026, with RBI approval received and staff mobilised.

Plans to open 200 branches, expand the BC network from 3,027 to more than 4,000 by year end, and launch UnIC 2.0 digital platform by FY27 end. IT budget to roughly double; resilience operations centre due in 3-4 months.
capex_capacity: Business per branch is around Rs.158 crore, still well below the industry average. A global consultant has been engaged for branch rationalisation and new locations.
Organisational restructuring added three zonal offices (Kolkata, Delhi, Lucknow) and four regional offices (Raipur, Bangalore, Shimla, Bhubaneswar), taking the total to 33 regional offices.
Business correspondent network at 3,027, to be scaled to more than 4,000 by end of FY27.
Resilience operations centre for cyber security due in 3-4 months. IT and AI/cyber budget being increased about 2x.
Navjyoti phase 2 (skill building) under way with BCG. A Chandigarh training centre of excellence opened, with about 125 scale IV-VI officers selected for leadership grooming.
demand_pricing: April sanctions remain strong: MSME sanction rate described as strong and retail sanctions growing over 25%. Management said the outlook is a mixed bag, with leads rising in data centres, logistics, infrastructure, LRDs and renewables.
Management does not see any challenge to FY27 guidance. It said geopolitical stress is not yet visible in the book, though small MSMEs could be hit if the conflict lingers. Forex exposure is limited.
NIM pressure was driven by low CASA and repo rate cuts totalling 125 bps, which management says are now fully absorbed. Management expects the yield cycle to turn upward.
Treasury could see a favourable write-back if bond yields soften as the Gulf situation improves.

qa_highlights.question: What is the plan for ECL implementation from April 2027, and how much buffer exists?
qa_highlights.answer: The CRO said the impact is estimated at Rs.600-800 crore, spread over five years to FY31 with EIR from FY30. Management said it can be absorbed from the capital buffer without much effect on capital adequacy. Final calculations are pending.

qa_highlights.question: Why did Q4 slippages rise to Rs.355 crore while SMA-2 fell to Rs.96 crore?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said residual stress in agri and MSME led to downgrades under IRAC norms, which it chose to recognise early. SMA-2 above Rs.5 crore fell sharply, and SMA book is 4.21% including two state-guaranteed accounts (about 3% excluding them). One state account cleared dues in April.

qa_highlights.question: What is the path to a higher NIM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management guided NIM to 2.65-2.70% by end of FY27, driven by RAM mix, co-lending of over Rs.10,000 crore, and selective corporate pricing. It also cited historically low CASA as the main constraint.

qa_highlights.question: Is growth too slow relative to peers, and is there a plan to accelerate?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said growth must be qualitative. It targets Rs.3,00,000 crore business this year and Rs.4,00,000 crore by FY29, with about Rs.50,000 crore to be added each year, supported by 200 new branches, a marketing vertical and tab banking.

qa_highlights.question: What are the gold loan and CRM drivers, and what tie-ups exist for vehicles and housing?
qa_highlights.answer: Gold loans are growing over 100% organically, with co-lending also in use. Management cited about 85 housing builder tie-ups, Mahindra and Maruti vehicle tie-ups, and a new second-hand vehicle digital product still in pipeline.

qa_highlights.question: Is training and L&D set up as a separate function?
qa_highlights.answer: Management said L&D sits within HR for now and a separate vertical will be decided at an appropriate time. Navjyoti phase 2 is running with BCG, and tie-ups exist with NIBSCOM, IIMs, MDIs and SBI Academy.

risks_watch: MSME stress: Q4 slippages rose to Rs.355 crore from Rs.168 crore in Q3, and management said small MSMEs could be hit if the geopolitical conflict lingers. Track MSME slippages and SMA-1/SMA-2 movement in Q1 FY27.

ECL transition: capital impact estimated at Rs.600-800 crore over five years to FY31 (EIR from FY30), with final calculations still pending. Watch for the final quantification and any change to the capital adequacy position.
NIM path: FY26 NIM was 2.55%, declining quarter on quarter, and the guided 2.65-2.70% by FY27-end depends on CASA mobilisation and a RAM mix shift. Monitor quarterly NIM and CASA ratio.
Concentration in state-government-guaranteed SMA accounts: SMA book is 4.21% including two such accounts, about 3% excluding them, and the bank said these accounts can slip and re-enter the cycle.

Execution on expansion: 200 new branches, BC network from 3,027 to over 4,000, UnIC 2.0 launch by FY27-end, GIFT City branch by October 2026, and IT budget roughly doubled. Management admitted it fell just short of FY26 Net NPA and PCR guidance.
key_quotes: So the total business of the bank has grown by 14.94%, a historic growth for Punjab and Sind Bank, and it has touched Rs .2,63,652 Crore for the financial year.
There are some of the weak accounts which we thought best to recognize and move ahead.
So we feel that by the end of the current year, we should be touching 2.65 % to 2.70% in terms of the NIM.
As far as creating a separate vertical is concerned. We'll take that call at an appropriate time.
summary.management_tone: Confident on FY26 headline numbers and FY27 guidance, with management saying it sees no challenge to targets. Cautious on MSME and agri stress, geopolitical impact and NIM, and it deferred detail on the RBI ECL circular (CRO said final calculations are pending).

adds.what: 200 new branches planned (business per branch ~Rs.158 crore)
Business correspondent network expansion from 3,027 to more than 4,000

growth.why: FY27 guidance of 16-18% advances growth and 13-14% deposit growth, backed partially by a Rs.18,000 crore corporate pipeline (up from Rs.10-12k), over Rs.10,000 crore co-lending platform, April sanctions strong, and plans for 200 branches and BC expansion to 4,000+; no explicit capacity utilisation or detailed timing given.
